name: Tinted lip balm for men
lead: Tinted lip balm is a hybrid cosmetic that combines the moisturising and protective role of ordinary lip balm with a sheer, buildable wash of colour.[1] Men who use it are generally seeking a subtly healthier or more even lip tone without the opacity of lipstick; the entry is treated here as part of grooming and style culture.

Product descriptions in the available source emphasise hydration, a lightweight texture and a natural finish.[1] No clinical studies have been found that test tinted balms for appearance in men, so the evidence is limited to product descriptions.
infobox: Waxes, butters, plant oils, sheer pigments

paras: Tinted balms sit between colourless lip balm, which adds no colour, and lipstick, which gives fuller coverage with less emphasis on moisture.[1] Common ingredients cited include shea butter, plant oils and hyaluronic acid.[1] Compared with lip gloss they are described as less shiny, and compared with lip stains as more hydrating but less long-lasting.[1]

The source describes precursors in the late twentieth century such as tinted petroleum jellies, and cites Clinique Almost Lipstick (1971 as a gloss, relaunched in 1989 as a stick) as an early hybrid product.[1] Lip balm itself has a longer history, with ChapStick developed in the 1880s and sold commercially from 1912.[2]

The brief for this entry describes tinted balm as a way to boost natural lip colour. Sources reviewed describe the products in general terms and do not give male-specific data or marketing history.[1]

No studies found on tinted balm for appearance. A 2015 study of regular lip balm use, reported to have been funded by a manufacturer, found improved lip hydration and barrier function over two weeks.[2]

timeline.event: Clinique launches the sheer gloss later reformulated as Almost Lipstick.[1]
Almost Lipstick relaunched in stick form.[1]

card.summary: Moisturising balm with a sheer wash of colour; a low-stakes grooming product with no appearance trials.
card.note: Product descriptions only; some ingredients and fragrances can irritate sensitive lips.

quick.overview:
Tinted lip balm adds a light, buildable colour to a moisturising balm. People use it to even out or warm up lip tone without wearing lipstick.

No studies have tested it for appearance in men; information comes from product descriptions.
quick.mechanism: Sheer pigments are mixed into a wax, butter and oil base that coats the lips, giving colour and reducing moisture loss.
quick.risks: Generally a low-risk cosmetic. Dermatologists note some ingredients and fragrances can irritate sensitive lips.
